textPlacement.assessment: Pass for this exact r06 text and placement. “Sharing toys and taking turns” now clearly names the subject. Each actual short row explicitly identifies the baby using the object, allows the baby to be ready to move on, and tentatively names the baby’s wish to keep playing before explaining it to the other child. “That wish” now has a clear immediate referent; there is no ambiguous “them” and no instruction to lengthen a turn. The full detail retains both possible reactions and the reciprocal asking/waiting situation without forcing sharing or holding on. The first-year and around-12–16-month context appropriately qualifies the 6–9-month browse placement. The result is concrete, respectful and useful on its own short surface.

replacement.title: Sharing toys and taking turns
replacement.summary: If another child wants what your baby is using, notice whether your baby seems ready to move on. If your baby seems to want to keep playing, you can explain that wish to the other child.

issueResolutions.resolution: Resolved after reading the exact new title and summary together in both r06 topic rows and the full entry, and comparing with the full original sharing unit including its PDF 215 continuation. The baby’s actual interest and the other child are explicit; tentative interpretation and moving on are present in each short row. The new subject title removes the implied adult aim of prolonging the turn.
